subject: Service interruption impacting Streamline Payments - request for SLO credit
messages:
From: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@streamlinepay.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@streamlinepay.com, Emily Cho <emily.cho@streamlinepay.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Urgent] Redwood service interruption affecting checkout (SLO credit request)

Hi Vanessa,

We saw a service interruption this morning that impacted our checkout flow between 08:57 and 09:23 PT. During that window we observed ~22% 503s from calls to your text-generation endpoint (model-redwood/small-latency) and several failed authorizations for 2XX -> downstream payment verification. This impacted a handful of live transactions and triggered throttling on our side.

Can you confirm the downtime window and whether this is eligible for an SLA credit? We need:
- the official downtime start/end timestamps from your side (with timezone)
- a short summary of root cause if available or when the RCA will be delivered
- any recommended remediation steps we should take to avoid recurrence (we use pinned model version + client-side retry with exponential backoff)

This is blocking our finance ops reconciliation; if we can get a preliminary confirmation today that the window qualifies, we can start internal crediting processes.

Thanks,
Alex Dunne
Head of Integrations
Streamline Payments

Attachments: (1) sample-failed-request-logs.json

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@streamlinepay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 09:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Redwood service interruption affecting checkout (SLO credit request)

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and really sorry about the disruption. I’m escalating this to our SRE/eng on call now and cc’ing Marissa from CS so she can surface this internally.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- I’ve opened INC-4921 and asked Eng to pull raw trace bundles and token-level logs for 08:45–09:45 PT.
- We’ll attempt a preliminary downtime window confirmation within 2 hours and follow up with an eligibility assessment for SLO credit.
- Please send any additional sample request IDs or spans you have (the sample-failed-request-logs.json you attached is helpful).

I’ll follow up shortly with an ETA for the raw trace bundle and a proposed credit calculation.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.ai

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Streamline Payments — urgent: verify downtime window + gather raw traces (INC-4921)

Ben/Priyom — Alex at Streamline reports a ~26 minute spike of 503s impacting checkout between ~08:57–09:23 PT. Customer has provided a sample failed request and is asking for SLO eligibility and credit calculation.

Can you please:
1) Confirm whether Redwood observed a service-level availability gap on 2028-04-17 in us-west-2 for model 'model-redwood/small-latency' and give precise start/end timestamps (UTC and PT).
2) Bundle raw traces (service side spans, token-level logs, route decisions) and KV-cache hits for 08:45–09:45 PT and upload to the incident attachment (attach filename raw-traces-20280417.tar.gz).
3) Note whether routing fallback or model variant substitution occurred (we suspect a misrouted fallback to a quantized variant without proper kernel mapping that increased tail latency and triggered 503 throttling).
4) Provide a preliminary credit estimate using our standard pro-rata by uptime impact (include the formula used).

Customer wants a preliminary confirmation within 2 hours. If you need to rehydrate longer retention logs let me know and I’ll authorize an extended pull.

Thanks — this is high priority.
—Vanessa

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streamline Payments — urgent: verify downtime window + gather raw traces (INC-4921)

Vanessa — quick update from Eng: we verified an availability regression in us-west-2 for the 'small-latency' serving pool. Preliminary window: 2028-04-17T08:59:18-07:00 to 2028-04-17T09:21:44-07:00 (24m26s). Observed: increased token queue wait times followed by 503 responses when prefix cache miss rate spiked.

Root cause (preliminary): a routing policy change deployed as part of a capacity optimizer rollout incorrectly mapped a subset of requests to a quantized model variant that was only validated for shorter sequence lengths. When sequence lengths exceeded the tested threshold, the kernel selection path produced degraded throughput and elevated tail latencies which cascaded into request-time throttling.

I’ve uploaded the trace bundle and supporting artifacts here: raw-traces-20280417.tar.gz (s3://redwood-incident/INC-4921/raw-traces-20280417.tar.gz). The bundle includes:
- per-token latency histograms
- route decision logs (policy id=optimize-2028-04)
- KV cache hit/miss timelines
- sample request IDs that Alex shared mapped to spans

Preliminary SLO credit calc (subject to legal/finance sign-off): the affected window is 24m26s out of the 30d billing period for the customer’s monthly plan. Using pro-rata uptime formula: credit = (downtime_seconds / month_seconds) * monthly_invoice_amount. For Streamline’s $18,000 monthly invoice: (1466 / 2592000) * $18,000 ≈ $10.18 — we typically apply a minimum rounding policy and a service-level goodwill uplift depending on business impact; propose a $500 credit as an expedited remedy pending RCA.

If you want more precision (per-route token-weighted credit), we can run the per-route token accounting but that will take ~24 hrs.

—Ben

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@streamlinepay.com>, Emily Cho <emily.cho@streamlinepay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Redwood service interruption affecting checkout (SLO credit request)

Hi Alex / Emily — thanks for your patience while we validated. Below is the formal update and next steps.

Official confirmed downtime window (Redwood): 2028-04-17T08:59:18-07:00 to 2028-04-17T09:21:44-07:00 (24 minutes 26 seconds). This aligns with the request IDs you shared.

Summary of findings (short): a faulty routing policy rollout caused a subset of traffic to be routed to a quantized model variant without appropriate kernel mapping for longer sequences. That mismatch increased tail latencies and resulted in request-time throttling leading to 503 errors for a portion of traffic.

Preliminary remediation/mitigations completed:
- Deprecated the problematic policy and rolled back to the previous stable routing profile.
- Revalidated kernel selection for quantized variants and added sequence-length checks to the rollout gate.
- Enabled extended trace retention for this customer’s project to support deeper token-level accounting.

SLO credit and next steps:
- Preliminary credit calculation: pro-rata uptime formula yields a small numeric credit (~$10) but because of customer impact we propose issuing a $500 credit as an expedited customer remedy (this follows our internal goodwill policy for production outages that affect revenue-critical flows).
- If you’d like a per-route token-weighted compensation instead, we can run the token accounting job and provide a fully itemized credit (ETA: 24 hours).
- RCA delivery: we will provide a detailed postmortem (INC-4921) with timeline, root cause analysis, and corrective actions within 5 business days. A draft RCA is attached (rca-draft-INC-4921.md).

Please confirm if the proposed $500 credit is acceptable and whether you want the detailed per-route accounting. Marissa will follow up to begin any finance paperwork for applying the credit to your account.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep you updated as the RCA matures.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
